minutes.headline: Commissioners moved to pay for tank structural mapping from the maintenance account, toward a cell-carrier mast on the tank.
minutes.summary: The board heard that the state denied the appeal over PFAS pilot testing, planned public education on PFAS for a rollout around early 2024, and discussed a mast on the water tank for cell carriers. A motion to fund tank mapping and drawings from the maintenance account was made and seconded. The board also discussed reinvesting idle project money in a CD and objected to the engineer's change order on the Mass Ave main replacement.

what_happened.line: A motion to pay for tank mapping and drawings from the maintenance account was made and seconded; the outcome is not audible in the recording.
The board will wait out the 10-day window for any further appeal of the state's denial, then proceed with the PFAS pilot test as planned.
The board decided to tell the engineer it is not satisfied with its response or earlier work, and will not pay the Mass Ave change order yet.
Idle project money was reinvested in a six-month CD, at a rate somewhat above the borrowing interest, because the project was postponed.
The Mass Ave pre-construction meeting will be taken up at a commissioners' meeting, with documents signed outside the meeting.

why_it_matters: Water district spending that comes out of the maintenance account, and a possible cell-carrier mast on the tank, bear on district finances and on what ratepayers fund.
The Mass Ave main replacement change order is unpaid and unresolved, so its final cost to district ratepayers is not yet settled.
PFAS testing and the public education plan bear on drinking water quality and on what the district may later ask residents to fund.
